finding: XENO_PROMOTION_GATE/v2 stated that promotion inputs must come from bound executable benchmark receipts, but the executable CLI still accepted arbitrary raw JSON metric objects. A model/worker could therefore satisfy the mathematical anti-Goodhart comparison with unbound fabricated measurements.
hypothesis: Requiring a typed, digest-bound baseline/candidate XENO_BENCHMARK_RECEIPT/v1 pair before the existing epsilon-Pareto comparison closes the self-promotion gap without weakening the current cross-group anti-Goodhart semantics.
counterhypothesis: Receipt wrapping alone could become ceremonial provenance if the runner is not itself admitted. Therefore receipt integrity is explicitly classified as a deterministic provenance boundary only, not proof of runner trust, model causality, or whole-product runtime acceptance.
delta: preserve XENO_PROMOTION_GATE/v2 epsilon-Pareto, practical-significance floors, hard no-regression metrics, and cross-group progress
